newsitem.title: UK: Prudential shares up after ScotAm bid.
newsitem.headline: Prudential shares up after ScotAm bid.

text.p: Shares in Prudential Corp Plc climbed on Thursday in response to the British life and pensions giant's bid for mutually-owned life assurance group Scottish Amicable, dealers said.

The 1.9-billion-pound bid trumped an offer worth 1.4 billion from Abbey National Plc, and Abbey National shares were weaker in reaction to the news. Meanwhile, shares in Legal and General Group advanced on speculation that it could be next in line for a bid in the sector.
By 0850 GMT Prudential was up 13p at 567 and Abbey National 7-1/2p down at 774-1/2. Legal and General was up 9-1/2 at 403.
Lehman Brothers analyst Rob Procter said he had restated a strong "buy" recommendation for Prudential shares in the wake of the offer, and had a price target of 610p for the stock.

"I think this is a knock-out offer for Scottish Amicable which is unlikely to be matched elsewhere yet which offers good value to Prudential shareholders and Scottish Amicable policy holders," Procter said.
He said if the deal went ahead it would enhance Prudential's earnings by 2.5 percent in 1997 and 4.2 percent in 1998.
Market-makers said Legal and General's gains were fuelled by renewed speculation it could be the subject of an offer.
"This news has whipped up more bid speculation and people see Legal as the most likely target," one market-maker said.
